_style: Always address the user with respectful “તમે” (તમારું, તમને, તમારા) and never “તું”; for the couple together use “તમે બંને” / “તમારા બંનેનું”, and when the couple speaks about itself (garden, tree, shared titles) use inclusive “આપણું/આપણો/આપણી” (“આપણો બગીચો”), not exclusive “અમારું”. The other person is always “તમારા પાર્ટનર” with respectful plural agreement (“તમારા પાર્ટનરે મોકલ્યું”, “પાર્ટનર જોડાયા”), never પતિ/પત્ની/બોયફ્રેન્ડ/ગર્લફ્રેન્ડ/જીવનસાથી. Gujarati marks gender in past participles and many adjectives (ગયો/ગઈ, તૈયાર છો vs થયો/થઈ): keep sentences gender-neutral by using the respectful plural (“તમે પહોંચ્યા”), present tense, verbal nouns (“મોકલવાનું થઈ ગયું”), or rephrasing (“શું ચાલુ રાખવું છે?” instead of “તમે તૈયાર થયા?”); neuter agreement follows the noun (પત્ર is masculine: “પત્ર સીલ થયો”; યાદ is feminine: “યાદ સાચવી”; વૃક્ષ is neuter: “વૃક્ષ ઊગ્યું”). A partner’s name placeholder %@ is never altered or declined: postpositions may follow it as separate-feeling particles (“%@ સાથે”, “%@ માટે”, “%@ તરફથી”), and genitive/dative forms like %@નો/%@ને should be avoided by rephrasing (“%@ તરફથી પત્ર”, “%@ ને મોકલો” → “%@ સાથે શેર કરો”). Use curly quotes “ ” (inner ‘ ’), the single-character ellipsis …, a normal full stop “.” (not the Devanagari danda), no space before ? ! : ; and keep “ · ”, emoji, \n and every placeholder (%@, %lld, %1$@) exactly. Numbers in Western digits (0–9) as iOS formats them for gu, dates and times only via the system formatter; plural categories are ["one","other"] (CLDR “one” covers 0 and 1), and most nouns stay unchanged after numbers (“%lld દિવસ” in both), so “one” and “other” usually share the noun and differ only in verb or wording when needed. Gujarati script has no capitals: buttons are short polite imperatives ending in -ો (“સાચવો”, “મોકલો”, “ફરી પ્રયાસ કરો”), titles and tabs are short nouns without a trailing full stop; keep Latin-script brand terms Coupley, Premium, AI, CoupleSync, and common loanwords users know from iOS in Gujarati script (ચેટ, સેટિંગ્સ, શેર, વિજેટ, ક્વિઝ). Tone: warm, everyday modern Gujarati as spoken in cities, not Sanskritized or bookish, never syrupy.
